grade_reason: No statement by Turner about AI since January 2025 was found in news searches or on his official house.gov press release pages.
notes: All 7 web searches ran this time (the six required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act). No result showed Rep. Michael R. Turner (Ohio 10) saying anything about AI risk, superintelligence, a pause or slowdown, or a China agreement. Many results were about Alex Turner, a former Google DeepMind researcher, and Nicol Turner Lee, a Brookings witness; neither is this person. The site: search returned no turner.house.gov pages. The earlier run opened turner.house.gov/media-center/press-releases pages 0 to 6 (about 70 releases, 13 January 2025 to 21 October 2026); no title or excerpt mentioned AI (full text of each release was not opened). Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, sponsor Greg Casar): search results describe its House cosponsors as Democrats and none names Turner; the full Congress.gov cosponsor list was not opened. Turner sits on the House Oversight Committee, but the record of its 17 September 2025 hearing on AI ('Shaping Tomorrow: The Future of Artificial Intelligence', govinfo CHRG-119hhrg61734) shows he did not speak. As House Intelligence Committee chair he led a September 2023 committee trip to MIT that included AI policy discussions (intelligence.house.gov), but that predates 2025 and contained no quoted statement on AI risk.
